newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lufthansa plans global air cargo alliance.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa plans global air cargo alliance.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo is holding talks with several major airlines about establishing a global cargo alliance, Stefan Lauer, a member of the airline's executive board, said.

Speaking to reporters here, Lauer said negotiations include all member airlines of the recently-launched Star Alliance grouping, which includes Lufthansa, Thai Airways International, United Airlines, SAS, Air Canada and Varig.
Star Alliance is primarily focused on passenger integration, including code-sharing, but Lufthansa Cargo is keen to extend cooperation to freight too, said Lauer.

"I am sure we will see a cargo alliance on a global scale. Talks are underway with all members of the Star Alliance but we are not necessarily limited to those airlines," he added, emphasising that negotiations with possible partners are at an early stage.

"It is certainly my intention to globalise Lufthansa Cargo more. We are already big...we are the biggest. But there is still a lot of traffic flown where we are not able to participate, for instance trans-Pacific," Lauer said.
While he was in Hong Kong, Lauer would also be seeking to extend, to other areas, Lufthansa's long-standing cargo co-operation agreement with Cathay Pacific Airways on the Hong Kong-Frankfurt route.
"We have had a very important partnership with Cathay Pacific over the past 15 years and it is our intention to intensify that co-operation," Lauer said.
Lufthansa Cargo also has cargo co-operation agreements with Korean Air, Singapore Airlines, Japan Airlines and South African Airways SAA.CN.
